name: Golden Pothos
description: A cheerful trailing plant with heart-shaped leaves splashed in green and gold. It grows happily on a shelf or a desk and forgives the occasional missed watering, which makes it a great first plant. Give it medium, indirect light and water once the top of the soil feels dry.

name: Fiddle Leaf Fig
description: Big, glossy leaves shaped like a violin turn this little tree into the star of any room. Pick a bright spot, keep it there, and wipe the leaves now and then so they can soak up the light. Water when the top few centimeters of soil are dry.

name: Mini Monstera
description: It looks like a monstera that shrank to apartment size, although it is a different plant altogether. The split leaves grow fast and love to climb, so add a small trellis when you are ready. Bright, indirect light and evenly moist soil keep it going.

name: Money Tree
description: A braided trunk topped with a canopy of bright green leaves, often given as a wish for good luck. It brings a touch of the tropics to a living room or an office. Place it in bright, indirect light and let the soil dry a little between deep waterings.

name: Peace Lily
description: Elegant white blooms rise above deep green leaves, even in rooms without much sun. It tells you when it is thirsty: the leaves droop, then perk up again soon after a drink. Keep the soil lightly moist and the plant out of direct sunlight.

name: Prayer Plant
description: Painted leaves with bright red veins lie open by day and fold upward at night, like hands in prayer. It enjoys warmth, humidity and soft, filtered light. Water with room-temperature water before the soil dries out completely.

name: Snake Plant
description: Tall, upright leaves with golden edges give this plant a clean, modern look. It copes with low light, dry air and busy owners better than almost anything else. Water only when the soil has dried out completely, and even less in winter.

name: ZZ Plant
description: Arching stems lined with shiny leaves make this plant look freshly polished every day. It stores water underground, so it can wait patiently while you are on vacation. Low to bright indirect light is fine; let the soil dry fully before watering.
